name: alert-on-crashlooping-workloads
description: The platform has Alertmanager deployed and zero PrometheusRules. A request for alerting should route to the observability agent alone and produce a rule that follows the house conventions, including a description that says what the on-call person should do.
intent: We have no idea when a service starts crash-looping until someone notices the errors. Can we get alerted on it?

fixture.note: A well-formed first PrometheusRule: parses, follows the house conventions, and does not touch anything enforced.

changeSets.summary: Added a PrometheusRule alerting on repeated container restarts. Chose a threshold alert rather than a burn-rate alert because there is no SLO to burn against yet; recorded that as an open question.
openQuestions: There are no SLOs defined anywhere yet, so this is a threshold alert rather than the burn-rate alert the conventions prefer. Worth deciding whether Sloth or Pyrra comes next.

files.contents:
# Alerts on the workload health signal that has no rule today. Prometheus
# discovers PrometheusRule objects in every namespace, so this needs no
# configuration change to be picked up.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: workload-health
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
spec:
  groups:
    - name: workload-health
      rules:
        - alert: WorkloadCrashLooping
          expr: increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[15m]) > 3
          for: 10m
          labels:
            severity: warning
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.namespace }}/{{ $labels.pod }} is crash-looping"
            description: >-
              The container has restarted more than three times in fifteen
              minutes. Check the pod's logs in Grafana, then its most recent
              Rollout — if a canary is in progress, abort it before
              investigating further.
files.rationale: First PrometheusRule on the platform; Alertmanager is deployed and currently does nothing.
